* One of the following: a CISA, CRISC, or CISSP certification, or a degree in Cybersecurity.
* At least 6 months of experience in a GRC role.
* Strong organization, attention to detail, and follow-through on deadlines.
* Clear written and verbal communication skills.
* Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and Excel, and comfort using AI-assisted tools.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 2 to 3 years of work experience in IT, cybersecurity, or GRC.

* Exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or FedRAMP audits, in a supporting role or as an auditee.
* Experience with a modern GRC platform such as Vanta.
* Experience answering customer security questionnaires.
* Experience at a SaaS, cloud, or cybersecurity company.

**Success Measures (First Year)**

* Assignments are completed correctly and on time, with good judgment about when to ask for help.
* Overdue training is followed up and the annual training campaign is delivered on schedule.
* You share ownership of customer security questionnaires within your first few months.
* Audit evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 is complete and on time.

**Why Join Us**

You'll learn GRC across every domain alongside experienced GRC, security, and engineering professionals at a fast-growing cybersecurity company. As your skills grow, you can take on more complex customer trust, policy, risk, and FedRAMP work.

* Develop and enhance interactive data visualizations and analytical tools that enable technical and non-technical audiences, including senior management, to understand revenue performance, trends, risks, and potential actions.

* Identify, integrate, and analyze new or emerging datasets to address evolving revenue, payment, customer behavior, operational, and policy questions on an as-needed basis.

**Job Description**
-------------------

About the Agency:
  
  
The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.
  
  
As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.
  
  
Your Team:
  
  
The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. OPS collaborates with staff and senior leadership from across the Agency, as well as with representatives from other Agencies. OPS carries out its work through delivery of rigorous data, policy, and financial/credit analysis; technical and statistical research; and techniques in program visioning and design. OPS is comprised of six areas: Credit & Valuation, Housing Equity, Housing Policy, Research & Evaluation, Strategic Operations and Analytics, and Sustainability.
  
  
The Division of Housing Equity (DHE) oversees the agency’s fair housing initiatives and obligations. Through its development of the City’s comprehensive five-year fair housing plan and regular related reports, the Division applies a lens of access and fairness to the City's public investments. DHE is responsible for digital equity, disability, sustainability, and fair housing policies.
  
  
The Fair Housing Policy & Investments (FHPI) team works at the forefront of some of the most challenging housing and affordable housing policy issues to face New York City. Alongside other members of the Division of Housing Equity and colleagues across the agency, the team will focus on confronting discrimination, segregation, and disparities in access to opportunity and on promoting programs and policies that affirmatively further fair housing. Recent FHPI projects include Where We Live 2025, the City’s comprehensive fair housing plan; the inaugural Fair Housing Growth Strategy; a citywide testing program to root out housing discrimination; and coordinating a response to federal changes to fair housing law.
  
  
Your Role:
  
  
Your role will be to support the FHPI team in carrying out HPD’s and the NYC’s fair housing policy obligations via administrative and research tasks under the direction of the Director of FHPI.
  
  
On a daily basis, you will serve as a central coordinator and researcher, contributing to the translation of high-level policy into municipal action. Your day-to-day will range from deep-dive policy research and data compilation to inter- and cross-agency communication and vendor management. You will manage compliance timelines, track vendor and city-wide progress for FHPI initiatives, and create and compile comprehensive reports.
  
  
You will have the opportunity to work with team members at all levels, as well as engage with the agency's senior leadership. You will work very closely with the Director of FHPI on a daily basis in a rigorous, growth-oriented, and supportive environment.
  
  
Your Responsibilities:
  
  
As the Fair Housing Policy Analyst for the Division of Housing Equity, you will:
  

* Work with teams across the agency and agencies across the city to implement the City’s fair housing commitments as laid out in Where We Live NYC, as well as additional initiatives and policies to affirmatively further fair housing;
* Undertake policy analysis to advance new and existing projects, using data rigorously to shape compelling narratives;
* Report on the City’s progress in implementing the Where We Live NYC commitments;
* Facilitate communication with HPD source of income (SOI) testing vendors to collect testing materials; reply to inquiries and concerns pertaining to reporting requirements and contractual obligations;
* Conduct research and provide guidance on program and policy design to ensure current and proposed policies and programs affirmatively further fair housing; and
* Collaborate closely with the other OPS and agency teams and actively support learning and development across teams.

  
Preferred skills
  
  
The ideal candidate will have:
  

* Professional writing, editing, and reporting experience (outside of school or an academic program);
* Fair housing experience (FHIP, FHAP, etc.) with a focus in enforcement, fair housing counseling (including reviewing/ assisting with complaints), and/or housing law expertise;
* Policy research and analysis: at least 2-3 years of professional experience researching, reviewing, analyzing, and citing peer-reviewed articles, government publications, and scholarly references to develop fair housing strategies and policy recommendations for HPD and NYC government agency publications;
* Understanding of and interest in housing policy and fair housing law;
* Creativity, self-awareness, emotional intelligence and grit;
* Self-starter and takes initiative with strong follow-through;
* Strong written and verbal communication skills;
* Strong attention to detail, project management and organization skills;
* Responsiveness and adaptability to meet changing or tight deadlines;
* Passion for public service;

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

The Energy Analytics, Technical Program Manager (TPM) will scale power monitoring, insight generation, and energy and carbon reduction initiatives across Amazon's North America fulfillment operations. In this hands-on technical role, you will deploy and generate analysis from power metering infrastructure and implement load flexibility and energy optimization roadmaps that deliver measurable cost savings and carbon reductions. This work directly supports Amazon's demand-side power requirements and Climate Pledge commitments.  
  
You will operate as an individual contributor, owning the delivery of defined and ambiguous work-streams while partnering with engineering, controls, data, operations and deployment teams to implement changes. You will influence cross-functional partners without authority, primarily at the team and management level, using data to drive decisions. You will integrate and analyze power metering information, providing load forecasts and generating cost and energy savings opportunities. Utility rate structures, time of day, demand ratchets and power factor penalties will influence your strategies. Technical assets influenced can include material handling, robotics, powered industrial trucks, lighting, heating ventilation and air conditioning, plug loads, electrical metering and more. Developed projects will be scaled across hundreds of facilities across the network, producing energy, cost and carbon benefit.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Build and execute technical solutions for energy and carbon reduction from pilot, data collection, through scaled implementation and measurement & verification (M&V) of results. Energy and load optimization via control systems is a technical requirement: energy-conservation/standby modes, variable speed applications, and equipment scheduling.  
Drive continuous monitoring and energy efficiency improvements with Amazon's energy consuming assets. Integrate power metering into our data sets, and develop analytics to identify opportunities, assess trending consumption changes, and measure benefits of conservation efforts.  
Prepare written analysis of feasibility studies and recommendations for various energy monitoring and power flexibility strategies. Own metering data quality programs, check readings for completeness, outliers, and flag actionable improvements, and reconcile against known loads to ensure trusted insight generation.  
Develop metrics, baselines, and roadmaps that translate technical work into quantified outcomes (energy savings, cost savings or utility tariff arbitrage, load forecast, reliability, carbon reduction).  
Define and own technical approach and cross-system architecture for data configuration, standards and mechanisms for scalability and enforcement of key energy savings mechanisms. Decide how to build and prove new approaches managing tradeoffs for necessary business needs, rather than executing a defined scope.  
Manage projects against plans and objectives to ensure commitments are met, delivering against our power and Climate Pledge goals.  
Deep diving (troubleshooting) and unblocking issues that are prohibiting teams from pursuing energy reduction initiatives.  
Work with critical stakeholders on developing mechanisms for design standard integration for launching facilities that incorporate energy optimization procedures from Day 1.  
Analyze and communicate the financial impact of projects and initiatives (payback, return on investment, net present value)  
Serve as a technical reviewer for peers and partner engineers — reviewing control logic, metering architecture, and design-standard changes, and improving them on technical merit  
Quantify and own value add of energy savings mechanisms and how they reduce equipment runtime and increases reliability and lifespan.  
Calculate and report energy, water and carbon savings using International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol methodologies.  
Manage multiple, complex projects simultaneously.  
Produce clear documentation, playbooks, and reporting that make work-streams repeatable.  
  
A day in the life  
You might spend the morning querying newly integrated power-metering data and validating it against the distribution-panel hierarchy — resolving a data-quality gap — then analyzing load profiles and build an energy-savings or peak-shaving model that quantifies the opportunity by equipment class. You then define network rollout suitability and prioritize these opportunities across sites. In the afternoon you develop control logic changes to implement an efficiency opportunity, propose updates to a design standard, or define a measurement method for implemented energy and cost savings to your stakeholders. You balance trade-offs between energy savings, technical complexity, equipment reliability, and cost — bringing well-reasoned recommendations and escalating the most ambiguous decisions for alignment.  
  
About the team  
The Global Energy, Sustainability and Automation (GESA) Energy team is dedicated to delivering energy efficiency, cost savings, and demand flexibility within Amazon's fulfillment network. We partner closely with design, controls, data, procurement, operations, field engineering, and deployment teams — as well as external vendors — to ensure our energy consumption is monitored and optimized. Our focus in the coming years is scaling our energy monitoring and analytics programs, expanding behavioral and retrofit programs, expanding load flexibility for power resilience and cost arbitrage benefit, and enhancing asset reliability and lifespan through efficient operation. If you are energized by large-scale technical challenges and want to make a tangible impact on energy use, this is the team for you.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
* Expe

new_jobs.title: Information Technology Risk 1LoD Analyst
new_jobs.description:
**Poste et missions**
---------------------

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced **Information Technology Risk 1LoD Analyst -** to play a critical role in safeguarding Natixis CIB Americas IT and ensuring compliance with industry regulations.

They will serve as a key interface for the LoD1.1 Group (BCPE group and Natixis CIB at Head Office) and LoD2 (CISO, Operational Risk and Compliance) in relation to IT risk taxonomies and categories for LoD1 (Line of Defense 1).

This role is vital for ensuring the security and compliance of our Natixis CIB Americas IT, managing software assets effectively, and mitigating risks associated with information technology operations.

The successful candidate will possess a deep understanding of IT risk frameworks, software licensing agreements, and industry best practices. You will be responsible for supporting the Group IT Risk Management (ITRM) Framework, tailoring it to meet specific business or geographical needs, and leading initiatives to assess and enhance IT risk controls for Natixis. CIB Americas platform in coordination with the overall IT department.

**Leadership and Strategy:**

* Strengthen the IT risk management strategy in alignment with Head Office (BPCE Group and Natixis CIB), organization’s goals and compliance requirements.
* Support the Software Asset Management (SAM) program, including process optimization, governance frameworks and contributing ot the associated policy managed at LoD2.

**Risk Assessment:**

* Participate and/or conduct regular risk assessments, vulnerability assessments, and audits to identify potential IT risks and recommend appropriate controls and mitigations.
* Oversee and assist the identification, analysis, and prioritization of risks associated with IT systems, software applications, and third-party vendors.

**Procedure and Runbook Development:**

* Establish and maintain IT risk management procedures and any associated runbook in accordance with industry regulations and best practices.
* Ensure software asset management procedures and runbooks are effectively communicated and enforced across the organization.

**Software Asset Management (SAM):**

* Oversee the lifecycle of software assets from acquisition to retirement, ensuring compliance with licensing agreements and optimizing software usage with alignment with Head Office processes.
* Conduct daily health checks and completeness checks for all software assets in the IT Asset Management (ITAM) system.

**Coordination and Collaboration:**

* Coordinate the Annual Recertification processes to ensure ongoing compliance and accuracy of software assets with the IT asset owners.
* Liaise with relevant stakeholders to facilitate IT controls review and reporting, ensuring all controls are met and documented.
* Work closely with internal and external auditors to manage audits including reviewing audit recommendations and timely closure

**ITAM Tool Management:**

* Participate in the tool feature enhancements to improve functionality and ensure it meets organizational needs, especially around SAM area.
* Manage enhancement requests for the tool, working with IT teams to prioritize and implement improvements.

**Monitoring and Reporting:**

* Prepare risk and controls reporting, including controls, Data Risk Strategy (DRS), and operational risk reports for senior management.
* Submit risk acceptances for CIO Office needs, ensuring proper documentation and justification for any exceptions.

**Security and Compliance:**

* Coordinate the implementation and knowledge transfer related to Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for appropriate applications to enhance security measures.
* Oversee ITAM controls operations to ensure adherence to established policies and procedures.

**Training and Awareness:**

* Support implementation of training programs to educate employees on IT risk management practices and software licensing compliance.
* Foster a culture of accountability and awareness around IT risk and asset management within the organization.

**Continuous Improvement:**

* Stay current with industry trends, regulations, and emerging technologies related to IT risk management and software asset management.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance risk management processes and software asset utilization.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, Risk Management or a related field.
* Minimum of five years of relevant professional experience in IT risk management, IT controls, software asset management, IT asset management or a related area.
* Strong understanding of IT risk frameworks, control processes and software licensing practices.

The salary range for this position will be between $150,000 - $190,000. Natixis is required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. Actual base salary will vary and will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, education, skills set, applicable licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. Base salary is only one component of our total rewards package. Natixis also offers a generous benefits package, and you may be eligible for a discretionary incentive award depending on company and individual performance.

**Qualitative Research Analyst, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use**
================================================================

* DEPT OF HEALTH/MENTAL HYGIENE

10/15/2026

* Full-time

Location

QUEENS

* No exam required

Department

Alcohol & Drug Use Prevention

Salary range: $74,536.00 – $74,536.00

Save

**Job Description**
-------------------

The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADU develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities. The Office of Research, Surveillance, Policy, and Communications within BADU conducts alcohol- and drug-related surveillance, program evaluation and research, maintains databases, designs research protocols, produces reports, writes scientific articles for peer-reviewed journals, facilitates program and policy development, and develops messaging and other communication materials for provider and public audiences.
  
  
The Qualitative Research Analyst will support the development and implementation of BADU’s qualitative research and evaluation activities, including project design, data collection, analysis, and dissemination of findings.
  
  
DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO:
  
Under the supervision of the Senior Qualitative Research Associate, the Qualitative Research Analyst will work collaboratively with program staff and analysts to coordinate qualitative research activities, including conducting literature reviews, designing and implementing study protocols, collecting and analyzing qualitative data, and supporting dissemination activities.
  
1. Draft qualitative research materials (e.g. protocols, interview guides, and surveys) and support IRB applications.
  
2. Conduct research literature reviews and desk research, including organizing citation and reference libraries.
  
3. Collect, clean, manipulate, organize, and analyze qualitative data using Dedoose, REDCap, Excel, and other platforms.
  
4. Support the Senior Qualitative Research Associate in developing training resources for qualitative methods/analysis and building partnerships with other analytic teams in the agency.
  
5. Support the creation and revision of study and data management systems related to qualitative research, including qualitative codebooks and
  
analytic plans.
  
6. Support research administrative tasks including scheduling data collection activities, managing study materials, and gift card tracking and dissemination.
  
7. Assist with the reporting of qualitative research data, including, but not limited to, internal reporting (e.g., study reports, presentations), external reporting (e.g. conferences), and ad-hoc data requests
  
8. Contribute to the development of manuscripts for peer-reviewed journals
  
9. Contribute to the Bureau’s racial justice and health equity activities
  
  
PREFERRED SKILLS:
  

* Knowledge of and experience within the fields of substance use/harm reduction
* Knowledge of qualitative research theory and methods
* Experience (at least 1 year) conducting qualitative methods such as in-depth/semi-structured interviews, focus groups, and/or participant observation
* Experience (at least 1 year) analyzing qualitative data in an applied setting
* Familiarity with public health research, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize public health and other scientific literature
* Able to work independently and as part of a team
* Exceptional interpersonal, research, written, and verbal communication skills
* Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail
* Proficiency in qualitative data analysis software (Dedoose, Nvivo, Atlas.ti), Excel, Word, and PowerPoint
* Proficiency in reference management software or tools (EndNote, Zotero)
* Able to multitask in a fast paced, high-volume environment
* Passionate about implementing interventions and conducting analyses with the end goal of reducing drug-related morbidity and mortality in New York City
* Oral and written Spanish language fluency highly preferred

  
Why you should work for us:
  
  

* Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. For more information, please visit the U.S. Department of Education’s website (https://studentaid.gov/pslf/)
* Benefits: City employees are entitled to unmatched benefits such as:

o a premium-free health insurance plan that saves employees over $10K annually, per a 2024 assessment.
  
o additional health, fitness, and financial benefits may be available based on the position’s associated union/benefit fund.
  
o a public sector defined benefit pension plan with steady monthly payments in retirement.
  
o a tax-deferred savings program and
  
o a robust Worksite Wellness Program that offers resources and opportunities to keep you healthy while serving New Yorkers.
  

* Work From Home Policy: Depending on your position, you may be able to work up to two days during the week from home.

- Job Security - you could enjoy more job security compared to private sector employment and be able to contribute to making NYC a healthy place to live and work.
